output.name: Lethún — The Held Gull
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the gulls nearest the knife went first. One grey hen with a torn wing could not keep pace with the sky, so she hung behind, crying. Tavo the Gale came down the coast laughing and took her by the wing, turning her over like washing on the racks. Her wings went out stiff as sailcloth, and her body flattened thin as split cod. The Gulls carried her cry up to Mother Hesk. Tavo cannot be bargained with, so Hesk did not try. She counted every feather and wrote the count in the Spindle, so the gull would be held by the count, not the string. Now she hangs over the Windward Reach, head up, tail down. Vanu the skua waits on the wind to the north-west for gulls to dive, but this one cannot dive, so the thief has left her be. Ireth passes over her and never once asks her leave. My mother said to watch her when the wind is wrong. If she is still, the wind will hold. If she turns, bring the nets in.
output.finding: Start at Vanu, the Thief-Bird, and look a fist (about 9°) to the south-east to find Lethún, the Held Gull, in the Windward Reach.
